title: The Second First Meeting
description: Minjun already knows who Lim Sang-chul is. The broker who led his father into debt. Last run, he learned what kind of man this is. This time, he can use that knowledge differently. At the café window seat, Sang-chul extends a business card with a smile. Minjun knows what lies behind that smile.

choices.text: (He played dumb and sat down. He needs this man.)
choices.result_text: Minjun took the card as if seeing the name for the first time. He didn't realize how draining it was to treat someone you know like a stranger. But this man is the key to the network.
choices.foreshadow: Needing this man and knowing what he is — those two things can coexist. He decided to believe that.

choices.text: "Do you happen to know my father? The Kim family from Changwon."
choices.result_text: Sang-chul's expression hardened. After a brief silence, he slowly reached back for his business card. This relationship was going to flow in a different direction now. Strangely, what came first wasn't fear — it was a sense of relief.

title: Different This Time
description: He ran into Da-eun at the convenience store again. Last time he barely noticed her and moved on, but this time he knows how it ends. He knows what happened then, and what could have happened instead. If he doesn't want to repeat the same mistake, he has to decide right now.

choices.text: (This time, he was genuine from the start)
choices.result_text: Minjun didn't pretend to be busy this time. Da-eun seemed caught off guard. People don't usually get this real with strangers they've just met. But Minjun knows how much this beginning matters.

choices.text: (He walked past her, just like before)
choices.result_text: He walked past her again. The door closed, and only then did he feel the weight of that choice settle back in. There are some people you can't afford to let slip by twice — and he knew it.

title: This Time, He Calls First
description: Dad called. He got this same call last run. He was too busy then and cut it short. He knows what came after that. The day his father checked into the hospital alone, Minjun was in Seoul, staring at an investment app.

choices.result_text: There was a pause on the other end. "Alright... come." Just a few words, but his voice was different. The moment Minjun decided to go, something felt like it had found its place again.
A two-minute call. He set the phone down after. Last time he did this too. This time, exactly the same. Some things he knew he needed to change, but couldn't.

title: A Familiar Feeling
description:
Sangchul stood at the casino entrance. The sound of slot machines drifted out.
"You have to experience it yourself to know." He smiled and pushed the door open.

A strange déjà vu hit. Like vertigo — he knows this sound. This smell. This feeling.

He already knows what it feels like to lose everything.

choices.result_text:
He stopped at the door. Said nothing. Sangchul turned and looked — an expression he couldn't read.

"Later." Just that.

There's no way to explain that this isn't his first time. Not yet.

choices.text: (Goes in anyway. This time he can do it differently.)
choices.result_text:
He went in again.

"I can do it differently this time." He knew how dangerous those words were — and he crossed the threshold anyway.

title: He Remembered the Circles
description:
A night with nothing on the line.

Before, this quiet felt hollow. He needed something at stake to feel alive — opening the betting app, closing it, opening it again.

This night is different.

This is a night he can draw a circle on the calendar. He now knows why betting nothing feels so full.

choices.text: (Drew the circle. Starting from the beginning this time.)
choices.result_text:
One circle on the calendar. He knows how long it took to reach thirty in his previous life.

He started earlier this time. That alone was already different.

title: A Back He's Seen Somewhere
description:
Outside the convenience store. A man stared only at his phone over a cup of instant noodles.

A betting screen. A face lit by the glow. His hands trembled faintly.

{name} knows that back. Knows it far too well.
Some dawn in a past life, the same face was in the mirror.

He could pretend not to see and walk on. It's someone else's business.
But {name} knows where that road ends.

choices.text: Sit beside him and speak — "Hard to quit, isn't it."
choices.result_text:
The man flinched. {name} pulled two vending-machine coffees and held one out.

He didn't talk long. Just told his own story. The dawn he hit bottom, the gamblers' anonymous number, the circles on the calendar.

The man listened a while, then put his phone in his pocket. "…I'll give that meeting a try."

There's something only the saved can do. Reaching out a hand to the next person.

choices.text: Walk past quietly — my own road comes first
choices.result_text:
{name} just walked past. Wondered if he even had the right to step into another's life.

But turning the corner, that back kept weighing on him.
It felt like turning away from his own past self one more time.

Some debts remain not as money, but as a hand never offered.

title: Same Hands, Somewhere Else
description:
The hand that used to draw circles on the calendar.
That hand that filled in one each day, same time, same spot.

This time, {name} was using that hand to keep a household ledger.

The discipline of quitting an addiction didn't vanish — it moved elsewhere.
Ten thousand won saved every day. A portfolio review once a week. The same repetition, the same patience.

What he learned at the steepest price in a past life had become his greatest weapon in this one.

choices.text: Pour that discipline into building assets
choices.result_text:
What gambling taught him wasn't the 'one big hit' — it was compounding. Only now did {name} understand.

Like the circles he drew one a day, the money stacked little by little each month began to curve upward.

Slow. Boring. And — it never once collapsed.
The patience of someone who quit was the strongest asset of all before the market.

choices.text: Grow impatient — he wants to win it back fast
choices.result_text:
The patience that drew those circles sometimes leaked out as impatience.

'At this pace, when do I ever reach Gangnam?' Every time that thought came, it was dangerous.

{name} closed the phone. Impatience itself was the voice of an old friend calling the quitter back.
Slowly. He had to go slowly.
